newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar emir begins restructuring government powers.
newsitem.headline: Qatar emir begins restructuring government powers.

text.p: Qatar's emir has taken the first step towards restructuring the small Gulf Arab state's government by separating royal powers from those of the cabinet.

A decree issued by the Emir Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa al-Thani on Wednesday redefined the powers and jurisdiction of the emir as executive head of state and of the prime minister and cabinet as senior executive organ of government.

Under a provisional constitution in force since it was decreed in 1971 by the former emir Sheikh Khalifa bin Hamad al-Thani, the emir acted as his own prime minister. Ministers were appointed and fired at his sole discretion.
Sheikh Hamad, who took power from his father in a bloodless palace coup last year, on Tuesday named his 18-year-old third son as crown prince and heir apparent.
He has now separated the prime minister's office and the royal court or emiri diwan. Ministers will be appointed at the recommendation of the prime minister.
The decree rules that the cabinet will be collectively responsible to the emir for implementing the general policy of the state.

The emir will remain the supreme authority and will "lay down, in cooperation with the cabinet, the general policy of the state in all political, economic, social, cultural and administrative sectors."
"He endorses and issues laws and decrees and will have the supreme supervision over their execution in order to secure the rule of law," the decree stated.

The decree was the first public indication confirming speculation by officials and diplomats that the emir would relinquish his position as prime minister and appoint his brother, Sheikh Abdullah bin Khalifa al-Thani, to the post in a cabinet reshuffle next week.
Sheikh Abdullah, interior minister and deputy prime minister, helped his older brother topple their father in June 1995.
The reshuffle is widely expected to include the establishment of a supreme council of energy to replace the energy and industry ministry.
